report:
Baseline: independently compared current expr.rs, method.rs and semantic_spec.rs with the historical input snapshots; all three are exact byte matches, and the complete claim is unchanged. The captured historical rationale is a substantive, scoped TODO assessment, not proof of full implementation. I reassessed all current initial fragments and both test entries.

The claim requires child-version isolation for candidate matching and other speculation; failed operations must discard equalities, wakes and staged obligations, successful operations must commit atomically, and freezing must follow fallback and terminal obligation processing with no live work. The linked transaction rationale further distinguishes sole-child collapse from isolated concurrent candidates, freezes ancestors against writes, and exempts append-only stash allocation. Those broader guarantees remain within the explicit deferred verification matrix, not established by the single rollback example.

The ordinary expr.rs association is the expression-checking entry point: method calls delegate candidate resolution, then elaborate the selected call and publish its parameter environment when necessary; other relations use inference-context operations. It is not itself proof of global transaction or completion invariants. Captured method.rs context shows external signature matching creates a root child, performs receiver and argument matching in that version, discards on mismatch, and stages/publishes obligations only after successful matching. This supports the narrow regression scenario, without certifying all underlying transaction machinery.

The ordinary external_method_mismatch_discards_partial_generic_bindings test constructs a receiver with bool owner argument, a fresh caller variable and a char second argument. The captured SignatureTcx fixture has parameters [method generic E, bool], so the first comparison can establish a partial generic relation before the second fails. The visible assertions require rejection, Bound::None on the caller variable and unchanged root semantic revision; a leaked parent binding or revision would be detected. It does not observe wakes or obligations, successful commit, fallback, terminal diagnostics or completion registries.

The second associated test, sage_meta::todo::checking_body_isolated_completion, is explicitly TODO and has no behavioral assertions. Its comment retains the outstanding matrix: rejection without leaked generic bindings/wakes/obligations, accepted-candidate atomic commit, residual-obligation diagnostics, and empty runtime, wake queue, obligation registry and root transaction set on completion. Closing it requires concrete candidate success/failure fixtures with observable transaction effects and a completion fixture exercising fallback and terminal processing, with assertions on all four live-work registries before freezing. This is a justified remaining implementation/verification prerequisite, not passing evidence. No N/A entry exists. All claim aspects are accounted for by the narrow implemented example or this visible deferral; no edits are requested to the unchanged accounting.

Execution: ran review start, recorded additional method fixture/operation and RFD reads, compared snapshots, and recorded this report. No Rust edits, behavioral tests or build were run by this reviewer. The coordinator separately reports cargo build and 321 sage-meta tests passed; that is not my execution evidence.
